m.s: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss {cherrytom} with a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes until blistered. Meanwhile dissolve {stockpowder} in 350ml hot water per serve and keep it warm in a saucepan on low.
Slice {chorizo} into thin rounds and fry in a large deep frying pan over medium heat for 4 minutes until crisp. Lift out and leave the red oil in the pan.

Add finely diced {onion} to the chorizo oil and cook for 3 minutes until soft. Add {garlic*0.5} (crushed) for 30 seconds, then {arborio}. Stir for 1 minute until the grains turn slightly see-through at the edges.

Add the warm stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each lot is almost absorbed before adding the next. After 18 to 20 minutes the rice should be creamy and just tender with a little bite.

While the risotto cooks, heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan over high heat. Cook {prawns} with the rest of the garlic for 1 to 2 minutes a side until pink. Stir the prawns and {peas} into the risotto for the last 3 minutes.
Take it off the heat. Stir in {butter}, grated {parm} and the juice of {lemon}, then rest for 2 minutes. Serve topped with the chorizo, roasted tomatoes and chopped {parsley}.

l: Reheat with a splash of water and stir well. Best eaten within a day because of the prawns. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
g: Naturally gluten free. Check the stock powder and chorizo.
